name: Creator memberships & newsletters
one_line: Lets fans pay creators directly, by the month. Recurring income a creator owns, in exchange for the platform's ~10% cut.
sells: Hosting, payments and membership tools that let creators charge fans directly; the platform keeps a cut
customers: Independent creators — writers, podcasters, artists, video-makers — and the fans who pay them
suppliers: Cloud hosting, payment processors (Stripe), email delivery, and the creators' own audiences

revenue.metric: money fans pay creators through dedicated subscription/membership platforms (GMV)
revenue.note: No clean industry total is published. Built from the leaders: Patreon processes 'over $2 billion annually' and Substack runs at an estimated ~$450M in gross writer revenue (Sacra), plus smaller platforms. The platforms keep roughly 10% as revenue. The broader 'direct fan-payment economy' is estimated above $10B once big-platform memberships (Twitch, YouTube) are included — those sit under video platforms here.

structure.why: No single firm dominates the whole space: Patreon leads paid memberships and Substack leads paid newsletters, with many niche platforms (beehiiv, Ko-fi, Buy Me a Coffee) and low switching costs. Fees cluster around 10%.
structure.hhi_note: Shares aren't published on a common basis, so HHI is left null; the market is split across membership platforms, newsletter platforms and tip jars.

econ: Direct patronage and disintermediation: instead of selling the audience's attention to advertisers, creators charge their most devoted fans directly for a membership or paid newsletter. It trades reach for margin — far fewer paying fans than an ad audience, but recurring income the creator controls, minus the ~10% the platform takes for hosting, payments and discovery.
rank_basis: money paid to creators / gross creator revenue (company disclosures and Contrary/Sacra estimates, 2025)

companies.name: Patreon
companies.note: The clear leader in paid memberships: 25M+ paid memberships, ~300K creators, $10B+ lifetime payouts (Axios, 2025). Standard fee is 10%.

companies.name: Substack
companies.note: Leader in paid newsletters: 5M+ paid subscriptions (2025), ~50K creators earning money, valued at $1.1B (July 2025). Takes a 10% cut.

companies.name: beehiiv
companies.note: Fast-growing newsletter platform; charges a SaaS fee rather than a cut of subscriptions, and runs its own ad network for monetization.

companies.name: Ko-fi
companies.note: Low-fee tip jar plus memberships and a shop; takes 0% on one-off donations on its free tier.

companies.name: Buy Me a Coffee
companies.note: Simple tipping and membership tool popular with smaller creators; flat 5% platform fee.

products_note: Flagship features as of Nov 2026, checked against each platform's site and 2025–2026 coverage. Shares aren't published on a common basis, so companies are ranked by money paid to creators; Patreon and Substack are the documented leaders and the smaller platforms are ordered by reach, not exact revenue.
